problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2z\,dV
$$

where $R$ is the type I region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,1\le y\le x,\,x\le z\le 1+x+y}.
$$
worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2z\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}{\int }_{x}^{1+x+y}2z\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}{\int }_{x}^{1+x+y}2z\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}[{\int }_{x}^{1+x+y}2z\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}[{z}^{2}]_{z=x}^{z=1+x+y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}(1+x+y)^{2}-{x}^{2}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}(1+y)^{2}+2x(1+y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}{y}^{2}+2xy+2y+2x+1\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}({y}^{2}+2xy+2y+2x+1)\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[{\int }_{1}^{x}({y}^{2}+2xy+2y+2x+1)\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2xy+y]}_{y=1}^{y=x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}+x)-(\frac{1}{3}+x+1+2x+1)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-2x-\frac{7}{3}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-2x-\frac{7}{3}\,dx & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{4}+{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-\frac{7}{3}x]}_{x=1}^{x=3} \\  & =(27+27-9-7)-(\frac{1}{3}+1-1-\frac{7}{3}) \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$
